about: Appearance schema v10 (2026-10-22), from wave 9: garage_door_style (glass-panel and roll-up doors read differently from a solid one), entrance_arch (an arched entry), dormers (windows standing out of a pitched or mansard roof).

says.one: ONE building fills most of the space between the red lines (slivers of neighbours at the edges do not matter)
says.best_fit: two or more buildings share the space, but one of them clearly fits the mapped size (width and height): describe that one
says.none: you cannot tell which building is meant, or none fits the mapped size

target_hidden.says: how much of the target's street wall is hidden by trees, vehicles, scaffolding or frame edges

says.none: an ordinary box of flat walls with windows - most buildings, including plain modern ones with coloured panels and Victorians with one small turret
says.wavy_or_curved_walls: walls or a roofline that curve or wave
says.shiny_metal_cladding: facing of shiny or reflective metal sheets (NOT painted or coloured panels, which are ordinary)
says.glass_curtain_wall: mostly glass from floor to roof
says.tower_dome_or_turret_dominant: a tower, dome or big turret that dominates the building
says.rooftop_billboard_or_sign_frame: a large billboard or sign structure standing on the roof
says.church_or_temple: a church, temple or similar religious front
says.mural_covered: most of the front painted with a mural
says.odd_shape_other: any other shape a box-and-windows game drawing could not show

special_structure.says: a kind of building that looks the same everywhere and that a game would draw from its own model: a gas station (canopy over pumps), an open parking garage (decks without walls), a car wash, a drive-through fast-food restaurant, an auto repair shop (open bays), a supermarket or big-box store with a car park, a school, a fire station. none for houses, flats, shops and offices.

sign_text.says: the words on the building's main sign(s), as written (e.g. "WASH-DRY LAUNDROMAT"), or "" when there is no legible sign

homes_above.says: are there homes on the upper floors (curtains, balconies, bay windows, a residential look), as opposed to offices or storage

storeys.says: the number of storeys on the street front, counting the ground floor, counted from the rows of windows

says.flat: a flat roof, behind a parapet or cornice (most city buildings)
says.gabled: a pitched roof whose triangular end faces the street, or a false front hiding one
says.hipped: a pitched roof sloping down on every side
says.mansard: a steep roof slope above the top cornice with dormer windows in it

dormers.says: windows standing out of a pitched or mansard roof

says.painted_wood_rowhouse: a narrow 2-3 storey painted WOOD house, one home: ornate trim, ONE bay, a gable or false front, stairs up to the door. Not flats: one front door.
says.wood_or_stucco_flats: a 2-3 storey house or small block of 2-6 flats, wood or stucco: several doors or bells, square or rounded bays, garages often under. At most 3 storeys; 4+ storeys with bay stacks is bay_window_apartment_block.
says.stucco_house_with_garage: ONE home (one front door), 1-3 storeys, smooth stucco, a garage at street level, arched or picture windows. Several doors or bells: wood_or_stucco_flats.
says.bay_window_apartment_block: a 4-7 storey apartment block with STACKS of bay windows up the front and NO shops at street level (shops underneath: shops_with_flats_above).
says.brick_apartment_block: a 4-9 storey red, brown or buff brick apartment block, flat front, often fire escapes
says.spanish_stucco_apartments: a 3-6 storey stucco apartment block with arches, iron balconettes, tile accents
says.boxy_modern_apartments: a plain modern apartment box: flat render or siding, ordinary aluminium windows, garages under, maybe colour panels. Plain, not much glass.
says.sleek_modern_apartments: a newer apartment block with LARGE GLASS, dark or metal panels or timber, box bays, glass balconies. Glassy and sharp, not plain.
says.shops_with_flats_above: 2-4 storeys of HOMES over a row of SHOPS at street level (often bays, wood or stucco). The shops are the difference.
says.one_storey_shop_building: one or two storeys of SHOPS opening onto the street, each with its own door and window, a sign band or raised sign panel. A single big store or office (one entrance, offices, a chain pharmacy) is modern_commercial_box.
says.brick_warehouse_loft: a brick warehouse, loft or workshop: big industrial windows, plain parapet
says.modern_commercial_box: a plain modern NON-residential box (offices, store, school, garage): ribbon or aluminium windows, panels or render, no homes.
says.glass_tower: a high-rise with a glass curtain wall
says.chinatown_building: a Chinatown building: painted balconies, tiled eaves, red, green and gold
says.classic_stone_block: a 3-12 storey pre-war block in stone, terracotta or smooth cream/buff render with a flat ornamented front and a heavy cornice: apartments, a hotel, an office or a bank (homes_above says which)

says.none: not a 19th-century ornamented wooden house or flats
says.italianate: 1860-80s: a FLAT top on a deep cornice with big paired brackets, SLANTED (angled) bay windows, tall narrow windows with hoods, often a porch with columns
says.stick: 1880s: SQUARE bay windows, a false-front or gable top, thin vertical boards and sharp angular trim
says.queen_anne: 1885-1905: a corner TURRET or round tower, a big gable often with shingle patterns, curved bays, spindlework, a mix of textures

says.plain: flat wall, plain window openings, a simple coping or cornice
says.some: a moulded cornice, sills and simple window surrounds
says.rich: hoods or pediments over the windows, brackets, carved panels, pilasters, a deep ornamented cornice

wall_colour.says: the main wall colour of the upper floors, ignoring windows, trim and signs; a shaded white wall is still white. See colour_says.

trim_colour.says: the colour of the window frames, cornice and ornament where it differs from the wall (a painted lady's trim: white, cream, a dark contrast)

ground_colour.says: the ground floor's wall colour, if it is painted differently from the floors above

says.wood_siding: horizontal wood boards: thin parallel horizontal lines across the wall, often painted
says.stucco: smooth or textured render with no lines
says.brick: brick, painted or not: a grid of small joints
says.stone: stone or terracotta blocks or ornament
says.panels: large flat panels with visible joints (metal, fibre-cement, concrete)

says.tall_sash: individual tall rectangular windows, taller than wide
says.wide_picture: individual windows wider than tall, large single panes
says.grid: large industrial or office windows divided into many small panes
says.few_or_none: the wall above the ground floor has NO windows, or only one or two small ones across the whole front: a warehouse, a big store, a garage. Several windows per floor is never this.

garage_doors.says: garage doors (car-wide doors) on the target's street front

garage_door_colour.says: the colour of the garage doors, if any (white, wood brown, dark grey...)

garage_door_style.says: what the garage doors are: plain solid panels, frosted or clear glass panels, or a corrugated roll-up shutter

shopfronts.says: shopfronts (shop or restaurant windows with a door, a sign) at street level: none; one; several but not the whole front; all = the whole frontage is shops

says.full: the ground floor is almost all glass: big shop windows from pavement to fascia
says.partial: shop windows with solid wall between or below them
says.little: mostly solid wall at street level, small windows or doors only

says.fascia: a continuous band above the shop windows carrying the shop names
says.raised_panel: a raised sign panel at the top of the front (strip retail)

says.open_bays: wide open vehicle bays (auto repair, car wash)
says.loading_docks: raised loading docks with roll-up doors

entrance.says: the homes' or building's front door: at street level, or up a flight of steps (stoop); none_visible if the front shows no door

entrance_arch.says: is the front entrance an arched opening (a round-topped doorway or recessed arch)

says.bracketed_cornice: a projecting cornice held on visible brackets
says.plain_cornice: a projecting cornice or moulding band without brackets
says.brick_corbels: brick courses stepping out under the top
says.plain_parapet: the wall simply stops with a thin coping
says.sign_panel: a raised panel at the middle of the top of the front, above the roofline
says.gable: a pointed gable, or a false front hiding one
says.roof_overhang: a flat roof slab overhanging the wall

bays.says: how many vertical STACKS of bay windows project from the upper floors across the target's WHOLE street front, corners included. Count them in seen_bays first.

bay_shape.says: the shape of the bay windows, if any

says.none: no balconies. Fire-escape landings are NOT balconies (that is fire_escape)
says.balconettes: iron railings across the lower part of several windows, flush with the wall
says.projecting: platforms you can stand on, sticking out of the wall, on several floors

fire_escape.says: metal fire escape stairs/landings on the visible street wall

awnings.says: fabric or metal awnings or canopies over the ground floor

awning_colour.says: the main awning colour, if any

colour_panels.says: on a modern front: groups of windows set in panels of a different, often bright, colour

colour_says.cream: cream or ivory: white with a clear warm tint
colour_says.redBrick: red or red-brown brick, terracotta red
colour_says.red: a painted red, maroon or orange
colour_says.blue: any blue, pale or strong, blue-grey glass
colour_says.green: any green or teal, pale or strong
